title: Obama Presidential Library: White House Television (WHTV) and WHCA Audio/Visual Records regarding the G20 Summit in Hangzhou, China (September 3–5, 2016)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request access to and copies of all audiovisual records created, captured, or maintained by White House Television (WHTV) and/or the White House Communications Agency (WHCA) pertaining to President Barack Obama’s attendance at the G20 Summit in Hangzhou, China, between September 3, 2016, and September 5, 2016.

Specifically, this request includes, but is not limited to:

1. WHTV Video Footage: All raw video footage, master tapes, cut footage, b-roll, and audio/video recordings documenting:

○ President Obama’s arrival at Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport aboard Air Force One on September 3, 2016 (including, specifically, the much publicized tarmac disembarkation).

○ All bilateral greeting photo opportunities, "press sprays," and opening statements (e.g., bilateral meetings with President Xi Jinping, Prime Minister Theresa May, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President Vladimir Putin, and other heads of state). The 90 minute meeting between Putin and Obama was well documented in the media as the "stare down" meeting between the two men. This request is specifically requesting raw video footage, master tapes, cut footage, b-roll, and audio/video recordings of the Putin/Obama meeting. 

○ The official post-summit press conference held at the JW Marriott Hotel Hangzhou on September 5, 2016.

2. Audio Recordings: All sound files, audio feed tapes, and room audio captured by WHCA or WHTV during official proceedings, bilateral press openings, and press briefings during the specified dates in Hangzhou.

3. Shot Logs & Production Records: All associated video shot logs, slates, production logs, cameraman assignment sheets, and metadata listings for WHTV video cassettes or digital media assets recorded during the September 3–5, 2016 trip to Hangzhou.

II. Search Parameters & Keywords

To assist archivists in locating these assets within the Presidential record collections, suggested keywords and identifiers include:

● Events/Locations: Hangzhou, China, G20, Xiaoshan, JW Marriott Hangzhou, West Lake State Guesthouse.

● Offices/Units: White House Television, WHTV, White House Communications Agency, WHCA, A/V Pool, Pres-Video.

In the spirit of the Obama Library's "Digital First" ethos, I ask that priority be placed on uploading the video to YouTube. Thank you for the work that the Obama Presidential library does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Colin McMillan Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to Colin R. McMillan, who served as the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Production and Logistics from March 5, 1990, to December 11, 1992, under the George H.W. Bush administration.

Official Correspondence & Memoranda: Letters, policy directives, and briefing memos sent to or from Colin R. McMillan, including communications with then-Secretary of Defense Dick Cheney and/or former Secretary of Defense Frank Carlucci.
Calendar and Meeting Logs: Daily schedules, visitor logs, and agendas for his tenure (1990–1992).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Charles Kallas
